page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7H12 processor clocked at 2.6 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity totals 128.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent state, and provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark testing demonstrates balanced multi-threaded compute across middle-tier categories, paired with weaker single-core and memory throughput metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 31,756.69 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 9,518.0. Multi-threaded decompression reaches 135.7 GB/s in bzip3. However, single-core execution shows limitations, scoring in the bottom 10% on stress-ng at 764.29. Large-block memory operations fall into the lower 25% percentile, recording uncached read and write bandwidths of 35.29 GB/s and 16.62 GB/s respectively, while cached small-block reads reach 1,522.69 GB/s.

With steady multi-core performance, 8 Gbps network throughput, and average results in Redis operations (27.69 million ops/sec) and static web serving (7.46 GB/s), the ecs.g6a.8xlarge fits scale-out backend applications, enterprise web serving, microservices clusters, and continuous integration pipelines. However, workloads requiring high single-thread clock speed, extensive vector computing via AVX-512, or intensive uncached memory streaming will encounter hardware constraints on this platform.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor at 2.6 GHz, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) and 128.0 GB of RAM. Reflecting a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation, it delivers 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while containing no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show balanced multi-core throughput, recording a PassMark CPU score of 31,756.69 and Geekbench multi-core score of 9,518.0. Conversely, single-thread compute and uncached memory bandwidth show measurable constraints, with stress-ng single-core in the lower tier and uncached read bandwidth measuring 35.29 GB/s. With support for standard cryptographic and integer instructions without AVX-512, this instance is configured for distributed web servers, application tiers, container hosts, and balanced multi-threaded batch operations.
